Every point satisfying the conditions is on the locus and every point on the locus satisfies the conditions.
Every point not on the locus does not satisfy the conditions and every point not satisfying the conditions is not on the locus.
Every point satisfying the conditions is on the locus and every point not satisfying the conditions is not on the locus.

solutions.title: Contrapositives
solutions.body:
A correct proof must show two things: (i) on the locus $\Rightarrow$ satisfies, and (ii) satisfies $\Rightarrow$ on the locus. In (B), “not satisfying $\Rightarrow$ not on the locus” is the contrapositive of (i), and the second part is (i) again. So (B) proves only half; (ii) is never shown.

**Answer: (B)**

solutions.title: Check the others
solutions.body:
(A): (i) and the contrapositive of (ii). (C): (ii) and (i). (D): contrapositive of (ii) and contrapositive of (i). (E): (ii) and contrapositive of (i). All of these prove both directions; only (B) fails.

**Answer: (B)**

prompt: A number which when divided by $10$ leaves a remainder of $9$, when divided by $9$ leaves a remainder of $8$, by $8$ leaves a remainder of $7$, etc., down to where, when divided by $2$, it leaves a remainder of $1$, is:

solutions.title: Add one
solutions.body:
In each case the remainder is one less than the divisor, so $N+1$ is divisible by $2,3,\dots,10$. The least common multiple is $2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7=2520$, so $N=2519$ (the smallest such number).

**Answer: (D) $2519$**

solutions.title: Check the choices
solutions.body:
$59+1=60$ is not divisible by $7$; $419+1=420$ is not divisible by $8$ or $9$; $1259+1=1260$ is not divisible by $8$. $2519+1=2520$ is divisible by all of $2,\dots,10$.

**Answer: (D) $2519$**

prompt: A rise of $600$ feet is required to get a railroad line over a mountain. The grade can be kept down by lengthening the track and curving it around the mountain peak. The additional length of track required to reduce the grade from $3\%$ to $2\%$ is approximately:

solutions.title: Length from grade
solutions.body:
A grade of $g$ means the track rises $g$ feet per foot of track (approximately). At $3\%$ the track is $\frac{600}{0.03}=20000$ ft; at $2\%$ it is $\frac{600}{0.02}=30000$ ft. The extra length is about $10000$ ft.

**Answer: (A) $10000$ ft.**

solutions.title: Proportion
solutions.body:
Length is inversely proportional to the grade, so going from $3\%$ to $2\%$ multiplies the length by $\frac32$. Starting from $20000$ ft, the extra is half of that: $10000$ ft.

**Answer: (A) $10000$ ft.**

prompt: A stone is dropped into a well and the report of the stone striking the bottom is heard $7.7$ seconds after it is dropped. Assume that the stone falls $16t^2$ feet in $t$ seconds and that the velocity of sound is $1120$ feet per second. The depth of the well is:

solutions.title: Solve for the fall time
solutions.body:
Let the fall take $t$ s, so the depth is $16t^2$ and the sound takes $\frac{16t^2}{1120}=\frac{t^2}{70}$ s. Then $t+\frac{t^2}{70}=7.7$, i.e. $t^2+70t-539=0=(t-7)(t+77)$. So $t=7$ and the depth is $16\cdot49=784$ ft.

**Answer: (A) $784$ ft.**

solutions.title: Check the choice
solutions.body:
For $784$ ft: the fall takes $\sqrt{784/16}=7$ s and the sound $\frac{784}{1120}=0.7$ s, total $7.7$ s ✓.

**Answer: (A) $784$ ft.**

solutions.title: Sum and difference of cubes
solutions.body:
$(x+1)(x^2-x+1)=x^3+1$ and $(x-1)(x^2+x+1)=x^3-1$. So each big fraction is $\frac{(x^3+1)^2}{(x^3+1)^2}=1$ and $\frac{(x^3-1)^2}{(x^3-1)^2}=1$. The product is $1$ (wherever defined).

**Answer: (C) $1$**

solutions.title: Plug in
solutions.body:
$x=2$: first fraction $\frac{9\cdot9}{81}=1$, second $\frac{1\cdot49}{49}=1$. Product $1$, while (A) gives $81$, (B) $9^4$, etc.

**Answer: (C) $1$**

prompt:
The formula expressing the relationship between $x$ and $y$ in the table is:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6\\ \hline y & 0 & 2 & 6 & 12 & 20\\ \hline\end{array}$$
If $x =\sqrt{1+\sqrt{1+\sqrt{1+\sqrt{1+\cdots}}}}$, then:

solutions.title: Self-similarity
solutions.body:
The expression under the first root is $1+x$, so $x=\sqrt{1+x}$, $x^2=x+1$, and the positive root is $x=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}\approx1.618$.

**Answer: (C) $1 < x < 2$**

solutions.title: Bounds
solutions.body:
The nested values $1,\sqrt2\approx1.414,\sqrt{2.414}\approx1.554,\dots$ increase. If a value is below $2$, the next is below $\sqrt{1+2}<2$. So the limit is between $1$ and $2$.

**Answer: (C) $1 < x < 2$**

prompt: Of the following statements, the only one that is incorrect is:

choices.text: An inequality will remain true after each side is increased, decreased, multiplied or divided (zero excluded) by the same positive quantity.
The arithmetic mean of two unequal positive quantities is greater than their geometric mean.
If the sum of two positive quantities is given, their product is largest when they are equal.
If $a$ and $b$ are positive and unequal, $\frac{1}{2}(a^{2}+b^{2})$ is greater than $[\frac{1}{2}(a+b)]^{2}$.
If the product of two positive quantities is given, their sum is greatest when they are equal.

solutions.title: AM–GM
solutions.body:
By AM–GM, $x+y\ge2\sqrt{xy}$, with equality when $x=y$. So with a fixed product, the sum is *smallest* when the quantities are equal; it can be made as large as we like ($xy=1$: $100+\frac1{100}$). So (E) is incorrect. (A)–(D) are standard true facts; (D) is equivalent to $(a-b)^2>0$.

**Answer: (E)**

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
Product $16$: $4+4=8$, but $2+8=10$ and $1+16=17$. Equal quantities give the least sum, not the greatest.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: If $\frac{xy}{x+y}= a,\frac{xz}{x+z}= b,\frac{yz}{y+z}= c$, where $a, b, c$ are other than zero, then $x$ equals:

solutions.title: Take reciprocals
solutions.body:
The equations say $\frac1x+\frac1y=\frac1a$, $\frac1x+\frac1z=\frac1b$, $\frac1y+\frac1z=\frac1c$. Adding the first two and subtracting the third: $\frac2x=\frac1a+\frac1b-\frac1c=\frac{bc+ac-ab}{abc}$. So $x=\frac{2abc}{ac+bc-ab}$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{2abc}{ac+bc-ab}$**

prompt: If you are given $\log 8\approx .9031$ and $\log 9\approx .9542$, then the only logarithm that cannot be found without the use of tables is:

solutions.title: What we can build
solutions.body:
From the data, $\log2=\frac13\log8$ and $\log3=\frac12\log9$, and $\log5=\log10-\log2=1-\log2$. So we know the log of any number built from $2,3,5$ by multiplying and dividing: $\frac54=\frac{5}{2^2}$, $15=3\cdot5$, $600=2^3\cdot3\cdot5^2$, $0.4=\frac{2}{5}$. But $17$ is prime and can't be built from $2,3,5$.

**Answer: (A) $\log 17$**

solutions.title: Compute the others
solutions.body:
$\log2\approx0.3010$, $\log3\approx0.4771$, $\log5\approx0.6990$. Then $\log\frac54\approx0.0969$, $\log15\approx1.1761$, $\log600\approx2.7781$, $\log0.4\approx-0.3979$. Only $\log17$ needs a table.

**Answer: (A) $\log 17$**

prompt: $AB$ is a fixed diameter of a circle whose center is $O$. From $C$, any point on the circle, a chord $CD$ is drawn perpendicular to $AB$. Then, as $C$ moves over a semicircle, the bisector of angle $OCD$ cuts the circle in a point that always:

choices.text: is as far from $AB$ as from $D$

solutions.title: Isosceles triangle
solutions.body:
Let the bisector meet the circle again at $P$. Since $OC=OP$, $\angle OPC=\angle OCP$. And $\angle OCP=\angle PCD$ (bisector). So $\angle OPC=\angle PCD$, which are alternate angles, hence $OP\parallel CD$. As $CD\perp AB$, also $OP\perp AB$: $P$ is the midpoint of the arc $AB$ (on the opposite semicircle from $C$), the same point for every $C$.

**Answer: (A) bisects the arc $AB$**

solutions.title: Coordinates check
solutions.body:
Unit circle, $AB$ on the $x$-axis, $C=(\cos t,\sin t)$ with $\sin t>0$, $D=(\cos t,-\sin t)$. Direction $C\to O$ is $(-\cos t,-\sin t)$ and $C\to D$ is $(0,-1)$; their bisector direction is the sum $(-\cos t,-\sin t-1)$. The line $C+s(-\cos t,-1-\sin t)$ at $s=1$ reaches $(0,-1)$, which lies on the circle: the fixed midpoint of the lower arc.

**Answer: (A) bisects the arc $AB$**

prompt: If $r$ and $s$ are the roots of the equation $ax^2+bx+c=0$, the value of $\frac{1}{r^{2}}+\frac{1}{s^{2}}$ is:

solutions.title: Vieta
solutions.body:
$r+s=-\frac ba$, $rs=\frac ca$. Then $\frac1{r^2}+\frac1{s^2}=\frac{r^2+s^2}{r^2s^2}=\frac{(r+s)^2-2rs}{(rs)^2}=\frac{\frac{b^2}{a^2}-\frac{2c}{a}}{\frac{c^2}{a^2}}=\frac{b^2-2ac}{c^2}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{b^{2}-2ac}{c^{2}}$**

solutions.title: Reciprocal equation
solutions.body:
$\frac1r,\frac1s$ are the roots of $cx^2+bx+a=0$. So their sum is $-\frac bc$ and product $\frac ac$, and the sum of squares is $\frac{b^2}{c^2}-\frac{2a}{c}=\frac{b^2-2ac}{c^2}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{b^{2}-2ac}{c^{2}}$**

prompt: The area of a square inscribed in a semicircle is to the area of the square inscribed in the entire circle as:

solutions.title: Compute both
solutions.body:
Radius $r$. The square in the semicircle has side $s$ on the diameter, centered: its top corners satisfy $\left(\frac s2\right)^2+s^2=r^2$, so $s^2=\frac45r^2$. The square in the full circle has diagonal $2r$, so area $2r^2$. Ratio $\frac45:2=2:5$.

**Answer: (C) $2: 5$**

solutions.title: Reflect the semicircle
solutions.body:
Reflecting the semicircle and its square in the diameter gives a $s\times2s$ rectangle inscribed in the full circle, with $s^2+4s^2=4r^2$. So $s^2=\frac{4r^2}{5}$, and compared with $2r^2$ the ratio is $2:5$.

**Answer: (C) $2: 5$**

prompt: The medians of a right triangle which are drawn from the vertices of the acute angles are $5$ and $\sqrt{40}$. The value of the hypotenuse is:

solutions.title: Set up the legs
solutions.body:
Let the legs be $a$ and $b$. The median from the end of leg $a$ goes to the midpoint of leg $b$: its length squared is $a^2+\frac{b^2}4$. So $a^2+\frac{b^2}{4}=25$ and $b^2+\frac{a^2}4=40$. Adding: $\frac54(a^2+b^2)=65$, so $a^2+b^2=52$ and the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{52}=2\sqrt{13}$.

**Answer: (D) $2\sqrt{13}$**

solutions.title: Find the legs
solutions.body:
Solving the system: from $4a^2+b^2=100$ and $a^2+4b^2=160$ we get $a^2=16$, $b^2=36$. So the legs are $4$ and $6$, and the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{16+36}=2\sqrt{13}$. Check: $\sqrt{16+9}=5$ ✓ and $\sqrt{36+4}=\sqrt{40}$ ✓.

**Answer: (D) $2\sqrt{13}$**

prompt: Tom, Dick and Harry started out on a $100$-mile journey. Tom and Harry went by automobile at the rate of $25$ mph, while Dick walked at the rate of $5$ mph. After a certain distance, Harry got off and walked on at $5$ mph, while Tom went back for Dick and got him to the destination at the same time that Harry arrived. The number of hours required for the trip was:

solutions.title: Symmetry and Tom's distance
solutions.body:
Harry rides $d$ miles and walks $100-d$. Dick walks some $e$ miles and rides $100-e$; arriving together forces $e=100-d$ (both have the same total time $\frac{d}{25}+\frac{100-d}{5}$ only then). Tom drives forward $d$, back to Dick at mile $e$, then forward $100-e$: total $d+(d-e)+(100-e)=4d-100$ miles in the same time $T$. So $4d-100=25T=25\left(\frac d{25}+\frac{100-d}{5}\right)=500-4d$, giving $d=75$ and $T=3+5=8$ hours.

**Answer: (D) $8$**

solutions.title: Check the schedule
solutions.body:
Tom and Harry drive $75$ miles in $3$ h. Dick has walked $15$ miles. Tom drives back: the gap of $60$ miles closes at $25+5=30$ mph in $2$ h, meeting Dick at mile $25$ at $t=5$. They drive the remaining $75$ miles in $3$ h, arriving at $t=8$. Harry walks $25$ miles from $t=3$ in $5$ h, arriving at $t=8$ ✓.

**Answer: (D) $8$**

prompt: If the radius of a circle is a rational number, its area is given by a number which is:

solutions.title: Rational times $\pi$
solutions.body:
The area is $\pi r^2$. If $r\ne0$ is rational, $r^2$ is a nonzero rational, and a nonzero rational times the irrational number $\pi$ is irrational.

**Answer: (B) irrational**

solutions.title: Why the product is irrational
solutions.body:
If $\pi r^2=q$ were rational, then $\pi=\frac{q}{r^2}$ would be a quotient of rationals, hence rational — but $\pi$ is irrational. So the area is irrational (e.g. $r=1$ gives area $\pi$).

**Answer: (B) irrational**

prompt: Two high school classes took the same test. One class of $20$ students made an average grade of $80\%$; the other class of $30$ students made an average grade of $70\%$. The average grade for all students in both classes is:

solutions.title: Total points
solutions.body:
The total is $20\cdot80+30\cdot70=1600+2100=3700$ over $50$ students, an average of $74\%$.

**Answer: (B) $74\%$**

solutions.title: Weighted average
solutions.body:
The average lies between $70$ and $80$, closer to $70$ in the ratio $20:30$: $70+\frac{20}{50}\cdot10=74$.

**Answer: (B) $74\%$**

prompt: The expression $a^3-a^{-3}$ equals:

solutions.title: Difference of cubes
solutions.body:
$x^3-y^3=(x-y)(x^2+xy+y^2)$ with $x=a$, $y=\frac1a$ (so $xy=1$): $a^3-\frac1{a^3}=\left(a-\frac1a\right)\left(a^2+1+\frac1{a^2}\right)$.

**Answer: (A)**

solutions.title: Plug in $a=2$
solutions.body:
$8-\frac18=\frac{63}{8}$. (A): $\frac32\cdot\left(4+1+\frac14\right)=\frac32\cdot\frac{21}4=\frac{63}8$ ✓. (D) is the negative of (A).

**Answer: (A)**

prompt: The cost $C$ of sending a parcel post package weighing $P$ pounds, $P$ an integer, is $10$ cents for the first pound and $3$ cents for each additional pound. The formula for the cost is:

solutions.title: Count the additional pounds
solutions.body:
After the first pound there are $P-1$ additional pounds at $3$ cents each: $C=10+3(P-1)$.

**Answer: (C) $C=10+3(P-1)$**

solutions.title: Check values
solutions.body:
$P=1$ costs $10$ and $P=2$ costs $13$. (C) gives $10$ and $13$ ✓. (A) gives $13$ for $P=1$; (D) $C=9+3P$ gives $12$ for $P=1$; (E) gives $13$ for $P=2$ but $3$ for $P=1$.

**Answer: (C) $C=10+3(P-1)$**

prompt: The points $(6,12)$ and $(0,-6)$ are connected by a straight line. Another point on this line is:

solutions.title: Midpoint
solutions.body:
$(3,3)$ is the midpoint of $(6,12)$ and $(0,-6)$, so it certainly lies on the segment joining them.

**Answer: (A) $(3,3)$**

prompt: The difference of the roots of $x^2-7x-9=0$ is:

solutions.title: Quadratic formula
solutions.body:
The roots are $\frac{7\pm\sqrt{49+36}}{2}=\frac{7\pm\sqrt{85}}{2}$; their difference is $\sqrt{85}$.

**Answer: (E) $\sqrt{85}$**

solutions.title: Vieta
solutions.body:
$(r-s)^2=(r+s)^2-4rs=49+36=85$, so $r-s=\sqrt{85}$ (taking the larger minus the smaller).

**Answer: (E) $\sqrt{85}$**

prompt: When simplified, $(x^{-1}+y^{-1})^{-1}$ is equal to:

solutions.title: Common denominator
solutions.body:
$x^{-1}+y^{-1}=\frac{x+y}{xy}$, so its reciprocal is $\frac{xy}{x+y}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{xy}{x+y}$**

solutions.title: Numbers
solutions.body:
$x=2$, $y=3$: $\left(\frac12+\frac13\right)^{-1}=\frac65$. (B) gives $\frac65$ ✓.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{xy}{x+y}$**

prompt: Two equal circles in the same plane cannot have the following number of common tangents.

solutions.title: List the positions
solutions.body:
Two equal (distinct) circles can be separate ($4$ common tangents), externally tangent ($3$), or intersecting in two points ($2$). Exactly $1$ common tangent happens only for internally tangent circles, which needs different radii.

**Answer: (A) $1$**

solutions.title: Why not 1
solutions.body:
Internal tangency means the distance between centers is $|r_1-r_2|$, which is $0$ for equal circles — they would coincide (infinitely many tangents). So equal circles never have exactly one common tangent.

**Answer: (A) $1$**

prompt: If $m=\frac{cab}{a-b}$, then $b$ equals:

solutions.title: Solve for $b$
solutions.body:
$m(a-b)=cab$, so $ma=mb+cab=b(m+ca)$ and $b=\frac{ma}{m+ca}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{ma}{m+ca}$**

solutions.title: Check
solutions.body:
Take $a=2$, $b=1$, $c=1$: $m=\frac{2}{1}=2$. (D) gives $\frac{4}{2+2}=1$ ✓. Choices (A) and (B) still contain $b$, so they don't solve for it.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{ma}{m+ca}$**

prompt: An automobile went up a hill at a speed of $10$ miles an hour and down the same distance at a speed of $20$ miles an hour. The average speed for the round trip was:

solutions.title: Pick a distance
solutions.body:
Say the hill is $20$ miles. Up takes $2$ h, down $1$ h: $40$ miles in $3$ h, i.e. $13\frac13$ mph.

**Answer: (B) $13\frac{1}{3}$ mph**

solutions.title: Harmonic mean
solutions.body:
For equal distances, average speed $=\frac{2\cdot10\cdot20}{10+20}=\frac{400}{30}=13\frac13$ mph.

**Answer: (B) $13\frac{1}{3}$ mph**

prompt: If $y=f(x)=\frac{x+2}{x-1}$, then it is incorrect to say:

solutions.title: Check $f(1)$
solutions.body:
At $x=1$ the denominator is $0$, so $f(1)$ is undefined — it certainly isn't $0$. The rest are true: $f(0)=\frac2{-1}=-2$, $f(-2)=0$, and solving $y(x-1)=x+2$ gives $x(y-1)=y+2$, i.e. $x=\frac{y+2}{y-1}=f(y)$.

**Answer: (C) $f(1)=0$**

solutions.title: Self-inverse function
solutions.body:
$f(f(x))=\frac{\frac{x+2}{x-1}+2}{\frac{x+2}{x-1}-1}=\frac{3x}{3}=x$, so $f$ is its own inverse; that confirms (A) and (E). (B) and (D) are direct substitutions. Only (C) fails, since $f(1)$ is undefined.

**Answer: (C) $f(1)=0$**

prompt: The sum to infinity of the terms of an infinite geometric progression is $6$. The sum of the first two terms is $4\frac{1}{2}$. The first term of the progression is:

solutions.title: Two equations
solutions.body:
$\frac{a}{1-r}=6$ and $a(1+r)=\frac92$. Dividing: $(1-r)(1+r)=\frac{9/2}{6}=\frac34$, so $r^2=\frac14$, $r=\pm\frac12$. Then $a=6(1-r)=3$ or $9$.

**Answer: (E) $9$ or $3$**

prompt: The function $x^2+px+q$ with $p$ and $q$ greater than zero has its minimum value when:

solutions.title: Complete the square
solutions.body:
$x^2+px+q=\left(x+\frac p2\right)^2+q-\frac{p^2}4$, smallest when $x=-\frac p2$.

**Answer: (E) $x=\frac{-p}{2}$**

solutions.title: Vertex formula
solutions.body:
The vertex of $ax^2+bx+c$ is at $x=-\frac{b}{2a}=-\frac p2$; since the leading coefficient is positive, this is a minimum.

**Answer: (E) $x=\frac{-p}{2}$**

prompt: A house and store were sold for $\$12{,}000$ each. The house was sold at a loss of $20\%$ of the cost, and the store at a gain of $20\%$ of the cost. The entire transaction resulted in:

solutions.title: Find the costs
solutions.body:
House: $0.8\cdot\text{cost}=12000$, cost $15000$. Store: $1.2\cdot\text{cost}=12000$, cost $10000$. Total cost $25000$, total received $24000$: a loss of $\$1000$.

**Answer: (B) loss of $\$1000$**

solutions.title: Losses and gains
solutions.body:
The house lost $15000-12000=3000$ and the store gained $12000-10000=2000$. Net: loss of $\$1000$. (The percentages are of different costs, so they don't cancel.)

**Answer: (B) loss of $\$1000$**

prompt: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio $6:8:9$. Then:

choices.text: the angles are in the ratio $6:8:9$
the angle opposite the largest side is double the angle opposite the smallest side

solutions.title: Compare squares
solutions.body:
The largest angle is opposite the side $9$. Since $6^2+8^2=100>81=9^2$, that angle is less than $90^\circ$, so all angles are acute.

**Answer: (C) the triangle is acute**

solutions.title: Law of cosines
solutions.body:
$\cos(\text{largest angle})=\frac{36+64-81}{2\cdot6\cdot8}=\frac{19}{96}>0$, so the largest angle is acute (about $78.6^\circ$). Angles are not proportional to sides, ruling out (B); the smallest angle is about $41.4^\circ$, and $2\cdot41.4\ne78.6$, ruling out (D).

**Answer: (C) the triangle is acute**

prompt: If the base of a rectangle is increased by $10\%$ and the area is unchanged, then the altitude is decreased by:

solutions.title: Inverse factor
solutions.body:
New altitude $=\frac{1}{1.1}=\frac{10}{11}$ of the old one, a decrease of $\frac1{11}=9\frac1{11}\%$.

**Answer: (E) $9\frac{1}{11}\%$**

solutions.title: Numbers
solutions.body:
Base $10$, altitude $11$, area $110$. New base $11$ needs altitude $10$: a decrease of $1$ out of $11$, i.e. $9\frac1{11}\%$.

**Answer: (E) $9\frac{1}{11}\%$**

prompt: A merchant bought some goods at a discount of $20\%$ of the list price. He wants to mark them at such a price that he can give a discount of $20\%$ of the marked price and still make a profit of $20\%$ of the selling price. The percent of the list price at which he should mark them is:

solutions.title: List price 100
solutions.body:
Cost $=80$. Marked price $M$, selling price $0.8M$. Profit is $20\%$ of the selling price, so cost $=80\%$ of the selling price: $80=0.8\cdot0.8M=0.64M$, $M=125$.

**Answer: (C) $125$**

solutions.title: Check
solutions.body:
List $100$, cost $80$, marked $125$, sold at $100$. Profit $20$, which is $20\%$ of the selling price $100$ ✓.

**Answer: (C) $125$**

prompt: $\log p+\log q=\log(p+q)$ only if:

solutions.title: Combine logs
solutions.body:
$\log(pq)=\log(p+q)$ means $pq=p+q$, i.e. $p(q-1)=q$ and $p=\frac{q}{q-1}$ (with $q>1$ so that $p>0$).

**Answer: (D) $p=\frac{q}{q-1}$**

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
$p=q=2$: $\log2+\log2=\log4=\log(2+2)$ ✓, and indeed $\frac{2}{2-1}=2$. (C) fails: $\log1+\log1=0\ne\log2$; (A) is undefined.

**Answer: (D) $p=\frac{q}{q-1}$**

prompt: Angle $B$ of triangle $ABC$ is trisected by $BD$ and $BE$ which meet $AC$ at $D$ and $E$ respectively. Then:

solutions.title: Angle bisector theorem twice
solutions.body:
Order the points $A,D,E,C$ on $AC$. In triangle $ABE$, $BD$ bisects $\angle ABE$, so $\frac{AD}{DE}=\frac{AB}{BE}$. In triangle $DBC$, $BE$ bisects $\angle DBC$, so $\frac{DE}{EC}=\frac{BD}{BC}$. Multiplying: $\frac{AD}{EC}=\frac{AB\cdot BD}{BE\cdot BC}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{AD}{EC}=\frac{(AB)(BD)}{(BE)(BC)}$**

solutions.title: Areas
solutions.body:
Let each third of angle $B$ be $\theta$. Triangles $ABD$ and $EBC$ have the same height from $B$ to $AC$, so $\frac{AD}{EC}=\frac{[ABD]}{[EBC]}=\frac{\frac12AB\cdot BD\sin\theta}{\frac12BE\cdot BC\sin\theta}=\frac{AB\cdot BD}{BE\cdot BC}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{AD}{EC}=\frac{(AB)(BD)}{(BE)(BC)}$**

prompt: If $\frac{x}{y}=\frac{3}{4}$, then the incorrect expression in the following is:

solutions.title: Algebra
solutions.body:
$\frac{x-y}{y}=\frac xy-1=\frac34-1=-\frac14$, so (E) has the wrong sign.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{x-y}{y}=\frac{1}{4}$**

prompt: The sides of a regular polygon of $n$ sides, $n>4$, are extended to form a star. The number of degrees at each point of the star is:

solutions.title: Triangle on each side
solutions.body:
Each point of the star is the apex of a triangle built on one side of the polygon, formed by extending the two neighboring sides. The base angles of that triangle are exterior angles of the polygon, $\frac{360}{n}$ each. So the point angle is $180-\frac{720}{n}=\frac{(n-4)180}{n}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{(n-4)180}{n}$**

solutions.title: Check with stars you know
solutions.body:
For $n=5$ the pentagram has $36^\circ$ points: (B) gives $\frac{180}{5}=36$ ✓, while (A) gives $72$, (C) $108$, (D) $162$. For $n=6$ the six-pointed star has $60^\circ$ points: (B) gives $\frac{2\cdot180}{6}=60$ ✓, while (E) gives $30$. Only (B) survives both checks.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{(n-4)180}{n}$**

prompt: On hypotenuse $AB$ of a right triangle $ABC$ a second right triangle $ABD$ is constructed with hypotenuse $AB$. If $\overline{BC}=1$, $\overline{AC}=b$, and $\overline{AD}=2$, then $\overline{BD}$ equals:

solutions.title: Pythagoras twice
solutions.body:
$AB^2=AC^2+BC^2=b^2+1$, and also $AB^2=AD^2+BD^2=4+BD^2$. So $BD^2=b^2-3$ and $BD=\sqrt{b^2-3}$.

**Answer: (B) $\sqrt{b^2-3}$**

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
If $b=2$, then $AB=\sqrt5$, and with $AD=2$, $BD=1$. (B) gives $\sqrt{4-3}=1$ ✓; (E) gives $\sqrt7$.

**Answer: (B) $\sqrt{b^2-3}$**

prompt: If $\frac{x^2-bx}{ax-c}=\frac{m-1}{m+1}$ has roots which are numerically equal but of opposite signs, the value of $m$ must be:

solutions.title: Zero sum of roots
solutions.body:
Cross-multiply: $(m+1)(x^2-bx)=(m-1)(ax-c)$, i.e. $(m+1)x^2-[b(m+1)+a(m-1)]x+c(m-1)=0$. Roots $r$ and $-r$ have sum $0$, so the $x$-coefficient vanishes: $b(m+1)+a(m-1)=0$, $m(a+b)=a-b$, $m=\frac{a-b}{a+b}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{a-b}{a+b}$**

solutions.title: Use the ratio
solutions.body:
Write $k=\frac{m-1}{m+1}$. The equation is $x^2-bx=k(ax-c)$, i.e. $x^2-(b+ka)x+kc=0$. Opposite roots need $b+ka=0$, $k=-\frac ba$. Then $\frac{m-1}{m+1}=-\frac ba$ gives $a(m-1)=-b(m+1)$, $m=\frac{a-b}{a+b}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{a-b}{a+b}$**

prompt: In the figure, it is given that angle $C = 90^{\circ}$, $\overline{AD} = \overline{DB}$, $DE \perp AB$, $\overline{AB} = 20$, and $\overline{AC} = 12$. The area of quadrilateral $ADEC$ is:

solutions.title: Subtract a similar triangle
solutions.body:
$BC=\sqrt{400-144}=16$, so $[ABC]=\frac12\cdot12\cdot16=96$. Triangle $BDE$ (right angle at $D$) is similar to $BCA$ (right angle at $C$) since they share $\angle B$. With $BD=10$: $\frac{DE}{BD}=\frac{AC}{BC}=\frac{12}{16}$, so $DE=7.5$ and $[BDE]=\frac12\cdot10\cdot7.5=37.5$. Then $[ADEC]=96-37.5=58\frac12$.

**Answer: (B) $58\frac{1}{2}$**

solutions.title: Area ratio
solutions.body:
The similarity ratio of $BDE$ to $BCA$ is $\frac{BD}{BC}=\frac{10}{16}=\frac58$, so $[BDE]=\left(\frac58\right)^2\cdot96=\frac{25}{64}\cdot96=37.5$. The quadrilateral has area $96-37.5=58.5$.

**Answer: (B) $58\frac{1}{2}$**

prompt: A powderman set a fuse for a blast to take place in $30$ seconds. He ran away at a rate of $8$ yards per second. Sound travels at the rate of $1080$ feet per second. When the powderman heard the blast, he had run approximately:

solutions.title: Catch-up equation
solutions.body:
Work in feet: he runs $24$ ft/s. At time $t\ge30$ the sound has traveled $1080(t-30)$ ft, and he is $24t$ ft away. They meet when $1080(t-30)=24t$, so $1056t=32400$, $t\approx30.68$ s. He has run $8t\approx245$ yd.

**Answer: (D) $245$ yd.**

solutions.title: Head start
solutions.body:
At the blast he is $240$ yd $=720$ ft away. The sound gains on him at $1080-24=1056$ ft/s, so it reaches him $\frac{720}{1056}\approx0.68$ s later, during which he runs about $5.5$ yd more: $\approx245$ yd.

**Answer: (D) $245$ yd.**

prompt: If $\left(r+\frac1r\right)^2=3$, then $r^3+\frac1{r^3}$ equals

solutions.title: Cube identity
solutions.body:
Let $s=r+\frac1r$, so $s^2=3$. Then $r^3+\frac1{r^3}=s^3-3s=s(s^2-3)=0$.

**Answer: (C) $0$**

solutions.title: Factor
solutions.body:
$r^3+\frac1{r^3}=\left(r+\frac1r\right)\left(r^2-1+\frac1{r^2}\right)$, and $r^2+\frac1{r^2}=s^2-2=1$, so the second factor is $1-1=0$.

**Answer: (C) $0$**

prompt: The ratio of the perimeter of an equilateral triangle having an altitude equal to the radius of a circle, to the perimeter of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle is:

solutions.title: Compare altitudes
solutions.body:
Perimeters of equilateral triangles are proportional to their altitudes. The inscribed triangle's altitude is $\frac32R$ (the center lies $\frac23$ of the way down the altitude, at distance $R$ from the vertex). The first triangle's altitude is $R$. Ratio $R:\frac32R=2:3$.

**Answer: (E) $2:3$**

solutions.title: Side lengths
solutions.body:
Altitude $R$ gives side $\frac{2R}{\sqrt3}$, perimeter $2\sqrt3R$. The inscribed triangle has side $R\sqrt3$, perimeter $3\sqrt3R$. Ratio $2:3$.

**Answer: (E) $2:3$**

prompt:
In the table shown, the formula relating $x$ and $y$ is:

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|} \hline x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ \hline y & 3 & 7 & 13 & 21 & 31 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

solutions.title: Test the choices
solutions.body:
$y=x^2+x+1$ gives $3,7,13,21,31$ ✓. (A) gives $3,7,11$ — fails at $x=3$. (B) gives $3,8$ — fails at $x=2$. (D) gives $0$ at $x=1$.

**Answer: (C) $y=x^2+x+1$**

solutions.title: Differences
solutions.body:
The differences $4,6,8,10$ increase by $2$, so $y$ is quadratic with leading coefficient $1$: $y-x^2=2,3,4,5,6=x+1$. So $y=x^2+x+1$.

**Answer: (C) $y=x^2+x+1$**

prompt: In a circle of radius $5$ units, $CD$ and $AB$ are perpendicular diameters. A chord $CH$ cutting $AB$ at $K$ is $8$ units long. The diameter $AB$ is divided into two segments whose dimensions are:

solutions.title: Similar right triangles
solutions.body:
Let $O$ be the center. $\angle CHD=90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle), so $DH=\sqrt{10^2-8^2}=6$. Triangles $COK$ and $CHD$ are similar (right angles at $O$ and $H$, common angle at $C$): $\frac{OK}{CO}=\frac{DH}{CH}=\frac68$, so $OK=\frac{15}{4}=3.75$. The segments of $AB$ are $5-3.75=1.25$ and $5+3.75=8.75$.

**Answer: (A) $1.25, 8.75$**

solutions.title: Power of a point
solutions.body:
$CK=\frac{CO}{\cos\angle OCK}=\frac{5}{8/10}=6.25$ (since $\cos\angle HCD=\frac{CH}{CD}=\frac8{10}$), so $KH=1.75$. By power of the point $K$: $AK\cdot KB=CK\cdot KH=10.9375$, with $AK+KB=10$. The numbers $1.25$ and $8.75$ satisfy both.

**Answer: (A) $1.25, 8.75$**

prompt: When the sum of the first ten terms of an arithmetic progression is four times the sum of the first five terms, the ratio of the first term to the common difference is:
Given $12$ points in a plane no three of which are collinear, the number of lines they determine is:

solutions.title: Choose pairs
solutions.body:
Each pair of points determines a line, and no line contains three of the points, so lines and pairs correspond: $\binom{12}{2}=66$.

**Answer: (D) $66$**

solutions.title: Count from each point
solutions.body:
Each point is joined to $11$ others: $12\cdot11=132$, but each line is counted from both ends: $66$.

**Answer: (D) $66$**

prompt: $K$ takes $30$ minutes less time than $M$ to travel a distance of $30$ miles. $K$ travels $\frac {1}{3}$ mile per hour faster than $M$. If $x$ is $K$'s rate of speed in miles per hours, then $K$'s time for the distance is:

solutions.title: Time = distance/rate
solutions.body:
$K$ covers $30$ miles at $x$ mph, so his time is $\frac{30}{x}$ hours. (The other information is not needed for this question.)

**Answer: (D) $\frac{30}{x}$**

solutions.title: Avoid the trap
solutions.body:
$M$'s rate is $x-\frac13$, so $M$'s time would be $\frac{30}{x-1/3}$; choice (C) uses $x+\frac13$, which is neither. $K$'s own time is simply $\frac{30}{x}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{30}{x}$**

prompt: A circle and a square have the same perimeter. Then:

choices.text: the area of the circle is the greater
the area of the square is the greater
the area of the circle is $\pi$ times the area of the square

solutions.title: Compute with perimeter $P$
solutions.body:
Square: side $\frac P4$, area $\frac{P^2}{16}$. Circle: radius $\frac{P}{2\pi}$, area $\frac{P^2}{4\pi}$. Since $4\pi<16$, the circle's area is greater.

**Answer: (B) the area of the circle is the greater**

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
Perimeter $4$: the square has area $1$; the circle has radius $\frac2\pi$ and area $\frac4\pi\approx1.27$. The ratio $\frac4\pi$ is not $\pi$.

**Answer: (B) the area of the circle is the greater**

prompt: The price of an article was increased $p\%$. Later the new price was decreased $p\%$. If the last price was one dollar, the original price was:

solutions.title: Multiply the factors
solutions.body:
Original $x$: $x\left(1+\frac p{100}\right)\left(1-\frac p{100}\right)=1$, so $x\cdot\frac{10000-p^2}{10000}=1$ and $x=\frac{10000}{10000-p^2}$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{10000}{10000-p^2}$**

solutions.title: Test $p=50$
solutions.body:
Up $50\%$ then down $50\%$ multiplies by $1.5\cdot0.5=0.75$, so the original price was $\frac43$ dollars. (E): $\frac{10000}{7500}=\frac43$ ✓. (D) gives $1-\frac{2500}{7500}=\frac23$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{10000}{10000-p^2}$**

prompt: With a rational denominator, the expression $\frac {\sqrt {2}}{\sqrt {2} + \sqrt {3} - \sqrt {5}}$ is equivalent to:

solutions.title: Rationalize in two steps
solutions.body:
Multiply by $\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5$: the denominator becomes $(\sqrt2+\sqrt3)^2-5=2\sqrt6$ and the numerator $2+\sqrt6+\sqrt{10}$. Then multiply by $\frac{\sqrt6}{\sqrt6}$: $\frac{2\sqrt6+6+\sqrt{60}}{12}=\frac{6+2\sqrt6+2\sqrt{15}}{12}=\frac{3+\sqrt6+\sqrt{15}}{6}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac {3 + \sqrt {6} + \sqrt {15}}{6}$**

prompt: To be continuous at $x = - 1$, the value of $\frac {x^3 + 1}{x^2 - 1}$ is taken to be:

solutions.title: Cancel the common factor
solutions.body:
$\frac{x^3+1}{x^2-1}=\frac{(x+1)(x^2-x+1)}{(x+1)(x-1)}=\frac{x^2-x+1}{x-1}$ for $x\ne-1$. At $x=-1$ this is $\frac{3}{-2}=-\frac32$, so that value makes the function continuous.

**Answer: (E) $-\frac{3}{2}$**

solutions.title: Derivatives (L'Hôpital)
solutions.body:
Both numerator and denominator vanish at $x=-1$. The limit equals the ratio of derivatives: $\frac{3x^2}{2x}\big|_{x=-1}=\frac{3}{-2}=-\frac32$.

**Answer: (E) $-\frac{3}{2}$**

prompt: Two equal parallel chords are drawn $8$ inches apart in a circle of radius $8$ inches. The area of that part of the circle that lies between the chords is:

solutions.title: Circle minus two segments
solutions.body:
Equal chords are equidistant from the center, so each is $4$ in from it. Each chord subtends a central angle of $120^\circ$ ($\cos\frac\theta2=\frac48$). One segment has area $\frac13\cdot64\pi-\frac12\cdot64\sin120^\circ=\frac{64\pi}3-16\sqrt3$. The region between is $64\pi-2\left(\frac{64\pi}3-16\sqrt3\right)=\frac{64\pi}{3}+32\sqrt3=32\sqrt3+21\frac13\pi$.

**Answer: (B) $32\sqrt{3}+21\frac{1}{3}\pi$**

solutions.title: Sectors plus triangles
solutions.body:
Join the center $O$ to the four chord endpoints. The region between the chords splits into two isosceles triangles with apex $O$ and base a chord (base $2\sqrt{64-16}=8\sqrt3$, height $4$, area $16\sqrt3$ each) and two sectors on the left and right. The chords take up $2\cdot120^\circ$ of central angle, so the two sectors total $120^\circ$, area $\frac13\cdot64\pi=\frac{64\pi}3$. Total $32\sqrt3+\frac{64\pi}{3}$.

**Answer: (B) $32\sqrt{3}+21\frac{1}{3}\pi$**

prompt: The area of a trapezoidal field is $1400$ square yards. Its altitude is $50$ yards. Find the two bases, if the number of yards in each base is an integer divisible by $8$. The number of solutions to this problem is:

solutions.title: Sum of the bases
solutions.body:
$\frac{b_1+b_2}{2}\cdot50=1400$ gives $b_1+b_2=56$. With $b_1=8m$, $b_2=8n$: $m+n=7$ with positive integers. Unordered pairs: $\{1,6\},\{2,5\},\{3,4\}$, i.e. bases $(8,48),(16,40),(24,32)$. Three solutions.

**Answer: (D) three**

solutions.title: List
solutions.body:
Bases must be positive multiples of $8$ adding to $56$: $8+48$, $16+40$, $24+32$ (swapping the bases gives the same trapezoid shape data, and $28+28$ is not a multiple of $8$). So there are $3$.

**Answer: (D) three**

prompt: If the perimeter of a rectangle is $p$ and its diagonal is $d$, the difference between the length and width of the rectangle is:

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
A $3\times4$ rectangle: $p=14$, $d=5$. (A) gives $\frac{\sqrt{200-196}}{2}=1$ ✓; (C) gives $\frac{\sqrt{150-196}}2$, not real.

**Answer: (A) $\frac {\sqrt {8d^2 - p^2}}{2}$**

prompt: In order to draw a graph of $ax^2+bx+c$, a table of values was constructed. These values of the function for a set of equally spaced increasing values of $x$ were $3844, 3969, 4096, 4227, 4356, 4489, 4624$, and $4761$. The one which is incorrect is:

solutions.title: Second differences
solutions.body:
For a quadratic at equally spaced points the second differences are constant. The first differences are $125,127,131,129,133,135,137$, and the second differences $2,4,-2,4,2,2$. The pattern $2,2,2,\dots$ is broken around the fourth value: replacing $4227$ by $4225$ gives first differences $125,127,129,131,133,135,137$. So the wrong value is $4227$, which is not among (A)–(D).

**Answer: (E) none of these**

solutions.title: Recognize squares
solutions.body:
The values are $62^2,63^2,64^2,\,?\,,66^2,67^2,68^2,69^2$, and $65^2=4225\ne4227$. All listed choices are correct squares; the incorrect entry $4227$ is not offered.

**Answer: (E) none of these**

prompt: Increasing the radius of a cylinder by $6$ units increased the volume by $y$ cubic units. Increasing the altitude of the cylinder by $6$ units also increases the volume by $y$ cubic units. If the original altitude is $2$, then the original radius is:

solutions.title: Check
solutions.body:
$r=6$, $h=2$: volume $72\pi$. Radius $12$: $288\pi$, increase $216\pi$. Height $8$: $288\pi$, increase $216\pi$ ✓.

**Answer: (C) $6$**

prompt: Let $D$ represent a repeating decimal. If $P$ denotes the $r$ figures of $D$ which do not repeat themselves, and $Q$ denotes the $s$ figures of $D$ which do repeat themselves, then the incorrect expression is:

solutions.title: Subtract
solutions.body:
From (C) and (B): $10^{r+s}D-10^rD=PQ.QQQ\ldots-P.QQQ\ldots$. The repeating tails cancel, giving $10^r(10^s-1)D=PQ-P$, where $PQ$ is the integer with digits of $P$ followed by $Q$. This is not $Q(P-1)$, so (D) is incorrect. (A), (B), (C), (E) just shift the decimal point.

**Answer: (D)**

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
$D=0.1\overline{6}=\frac16$, with $P=1$ ($r=1$), $Q=6$ ($s=1$). Then $10(10-1)D=90\cdot\frac16=15=16-1=PQ-P$, while $Q(P-1)=6\cdot0=0$. So (D) fails.

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: The diameter of a circle is divided into $n$ equal parts. On each part a semicircle is constructed. As $n$ becomes very large, the sum of the lengths of the arcs of the semicircles approaches a length:

choices.text: equal to the semi-circumference of the original circle
equal to the diameter of the original circle
greater than the diameter, but less than the semi-circumference of the original circle

solutions.title: It is constant
solutions.body:
Each small semicircle has diameter $\frac dn$ and arc length $\frac{\pi d}{2n}$. The $n$ arcs together have length $\frac{\pi d}{2}$ — exactly the original semicircumference, for every $n$. So the limit is the semicircumference (even though the curve gets closer and closer to the diameter).

**Answer: (A) equal to the semi-circumference of the original circle**

solutions.title: Scaling
solutions.body:
Arc length scales linearly: halving the diameter halves the semicircle. Two semicircles on the halves have total length equal to one on the whole, and repeating the argument shows the total never changes from $\frac{\pi d}{2}$.

**Answer: (A) equal to the semi-circumference of the original circle**

prompt: If an integer of two digits is $k$ times the sum of its digits, the number formed by interchanging the digits is the sum of the digits multiplied by

solutions.title: Add the two numbers
solutions.body:
Let the number be $10a+b=k(a+b)$. The reversed number is $10b+a$. Adding: $(10a+b)+(10b+a)=11(a+b)$, so $10b+a=11(a+b)-k(a+b)=(11-k)(a+b)$.

**Answer: (C) $11-k$**

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
$12=4\cdot(1+2)$, so $k=4$. The reversed number $21=7\cdot3$, and $11-4=7$ ✓.

**Answer: (C) $11-k$**

prompt: If $a$ and $b$ are two unequal positive numbers, then:

solutions.title: AM–GM–HM
solutions.body:
AM $>$ GM: $\frac{a+b}2>\sqrt{ab}$ because $\frac{a+b}{2}-\sqrt{ab}=\frac{(\sqrt a-\sqrt b)^2}{2}>0$. GM $>$ HM: since $a+b>2\sqrt{ab}$, we get $\frac{2ab}{a+b}<\frac{2ab}{2\sqrt{ab}}=\sqrt{ab}$. So $\frac{a+b}{2}>\sqrt{ab}>\frac{2ab}{a+b}$.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: The base of a new rectangle equals the sum of the diagonal and the greater side of a given rectangle, while the altitude of the new rectangle equals the difference of the diagonal and the greater side of the given rectangle. The area of the new rectangle is:

choices.text: greater than the area of the given rectangle
equal to the area of the given rectangle
equal to the area of a square with its side equal to the smaller side of the given rectangle
equal to the area of a square with its side equal to the greater side of the given rectangle
equal to the area of a rectangle whose dimensions are the diagonal and the shorter side of the given rectangle

solutions.title: Difference of squares
solutions.body:
With sides $l>w$ and diagonal $d$: the new area is $(d+l)(d-l)=d^2-l^2=w^2$, the area of a square on the smaller side.

**Answer: (C)**

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
A $3\times4$ rectangle has diagonal $5$. New rectangle: $9\times1$, area $9=3^2$. The given rectangle has area $12$, so (A), (B) fail; (D) gives $16$, (E) gives $15$.

**Answer: (C)**

prompt: In the set of equations $z^x = y^{2x},\quad 2^z = 2\cdot4^x, \quad x + y + z = 16$, the integral roots in the order $x,y,z$ are:

Two cyclists, $k$ miles apart, and starting at the same time, would be together in $r$ hours if they traveled in the same direction, but would pass each other in $t$ hours if they traveled in opposite directions. The ratio of the speed of the faster cyclist to that of the slower is:

solutions.title: Relative speeds
solutions.body:
With speeds $u>v$: same direction, the gap closes at $u-v$, so $u-v=\frac kr$; opposite directions, $u+v=\frac kt$. Then $u=\frac k2\left(\frac1t+\frac1r\right)$, $v=\frac k2\left(\frac1t-\frac1r\right)$, and $\frac uv=\frac{r+t}{r-t}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac {r + t}{r - t}$**

solutions.title: Numbers
solutions.body:
Speeds $3$ and $1$, $k=12$: same direction they meet after $\frac{12}{2}=6$ h ($r=6$), opposite after $\frac{12}{4}=3$ h ($t=3$). (A): $\frac{9}{3}=3$ ✓.

**Answer: (A) $\frac {r + t}{r - t}$**

prompt: In the figure, $\overline{CD}$, $\overline{AE}$ and $\overline{BF}$ are one-third of their respective sides. It follows that $\overline{AN_2}: \overline{N_2N_1}: \overline{N_1D} = 3: 3: 1$, and similarly for lines $BE$ and $CF$. Then the area of triangle $N_1N_2N_3$ is:

solutions.title: Three big triangles
solutions.body:
Let $[ABC]=1$. Since $CD=\frac13CB$, $[ADC]=\frac13$. Since $AN_1=\frac67AD$, $[AN_1C]=\frac67\cdot\frac13=\frac27$. In the same way $[BN_2A]=\frac27$ and $[CN_3B]=\frac27$. These three triangles do not overlap, and together with triangle $N_1N_2N_3$ they cover $ABC$ exactly (each is one small corner triangle plus one quadrilateral of the figure). So $[N_1N_2N_3]=1-3\cdot\frac27=\frac17$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{7}\triangle ABC$**

solutions.title: Coordinates
solutions.body:
Place $B=(0,0)$, $C=(3,0)$, $A=(0,3)$, so $[ABC]=\frac92$, $D=(2,0)$, $E=(1,2)$, $F=(0,1)$. Line $AD$ is $(2s,3-3s)$ and line $BE$ is $y=2x$; they meet at $s=\frac37$: $N_2=\left(\frac67,\frac{12}7\right)$. Similarly $N_1=\left(\frac{12}7,\frac37\right)$ (at $s=\frac67$) and $N_3=\left(\frac37,\frac67\right)$. By the shoelace formula, $[N_1N_2N_3]=\frac12\left|\left(-\frac67\right)\cdot\frac37-\frac97\cdot\left(-\frac97\right)\right|=\frac12\cdot\frac{63}{49}=\frac{9}{14}$, and $\frac{9/14}{9/2}=\frac17$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{7}\triangle ABC$**

prompt:
A line initially 1 inch long grows according to the following law, where the first term is the initial length.

$$1+\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{16}\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{64}\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{64}+\cdots$$

If the growth process continues forever, the limit of the length of the line is:

solutions.title: Split into two series
solutions.body:
Rational part: $1+\frac14+\frac1{16}+\dots=\frac{1}{1-\frac14}=\frac43$. Irrational part: $\sqrt2\left(\frac14+\frac1{16}+\dots\right)=\sqrt2\cdot\frac{1/4}{3/4}=\frac{\sqrt2}{3}$. Total $\frac{4+\sqrt2}{3}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{1}{3}(4+\sqrt{2})$**

solutions.title: Group in pairs
solutions.body:
After the first term, group $\left(\frac14\sqrt2+\frac14\right)+\left(\frac1{16}\sqrt2+\frac1{16}\right)+\dots=(1+\sqrt2)\cdot\frac13$. Adding $1$: $\frac{3+1+\sqrt2}{3}=\frac{4+\sqrt2}{3}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{1}{3}(4+\sqrt{2})$**

prompt: A boy buys oranges at $3$ for $10$ cents. He will sell them at $5$ for $20$ cents. In order to make a profit of \$1.00, he must sell:

solutions.title: Profit per orange
solutions.body:
Each orange costs $\frac{10}{3}$ cents and sells for $\frac{20}{5}=4$ cents, so the profit is $4-\frac{10}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$ cent per orange.

For a profit of $100$ cents he needs $100\div\frac23=150$ oranges.

**Answer: (B) 150 oranges**

solutions.title: Work in batches of 15
solutions.body:
Take $15$ oranges (a common multiple of $3$ and $5$). Buying costs $5\cdot 10=50$ cents; selling brings $3\cdot 20=60$ cents. Profit: $10$ cents per $15$ oranges.

A profit of $100$ cents needs $10$ batches, i.e. $150$ oranges.

**Answer: (B) 150 oranges**

prompt: A refrigerator is offered at sale at \$250.00 less successive discounts of $20\%$ and $15\%$. The sale price of the refrigerator is:

solutions.title: Multiply the factors
solutions.body:
A $20\%$ discount leaves $80\%$ of the price; a further $15\%$ discount leaves $85\%$ of that. Altogether $0.80\times0.85=0.68$, i.e. $68\%$ of \$250.00.

**Answer: (D) 68% of \$250.00**

solutions.title: Compute in dollars
solutions.body:
$20\%$ of \$250 is \$50, leaving \$200. $15\%$ of \$200 is \$30, leaving \$170. And $\frac{170}{250}=0.68$, so the price is $68\%$ of \$250.00. (Note the discounts do not simply add up to $35\%$.)

**Answer: (D) 68% of \$250.00**

prompt: The factors of the expression $x^2+y^2$ are:

solutions.title: Use $i^2=-1$
solutions.body:
$(x+iy)(x-iy)=x^2-(iy)^2=x^2-i^2y^2=x^2+y^2.$

The others fail: (A) gives $x^2-y^2$, (B) gives $x^2+2xy+y^2$, and (C) expands to $x^2+x^{2/3}y^{4/3}+x^{4/3}y^{2/3}+y^2$.

**Answer: (D) $(x+iy)(x-iy)$**

prompt: The roots of $x(x^2+8x+16)(4-x)=0$ are:

solutions.title: Factor completely
solutions.body:
$x^2+8x+16=(x+4)^2$, so the equation is $x(x+4)^2(4-x)=0$. The roots are $0$, $4$, and $-4$ counted twice (a double root), i.e. $0,4,-4,-4$.

**Answer: (D) $0,4,-4,-4$**

prompt: If $\log_6 x=2.5$, the value of $x$ is:
Charles has $5q + 1$ quarters and Richard has $q + 5$ quarters. The difference in their money in dimes is:

solutions.title: Convert to cents
solutions.body:
The difference is $(5q+1)-(q+5)=4q-4$ quarters, worth $25(4q-4)=100(q-1)$ cents. In dimes that is $\frac{100(q-1)}{10}=10(q-1)$.

**Answer: (A) $10(q - 1)$**

solutions.title: Test a value
solutions.body:
Take $q=2$: Charles has $11$ quarters, Richard $7$; the difference is $4$ quarters $=\$1.00=10$ dimes. Only (A) gives $10(2-1)=10$.

**Answer: (A) $10(q - 1)$**

prompt: The fraction $\dfrac{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}-\frac{x^2-a^2}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}}{a^2+x^2}$ reduces to:

solutions.title: Common denominator
solutions.body:
In the numerator, write $\sqrt{a^2+x^2}=\frac{a^2+x^2}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}$. Then the numerator is
$$\frac{(a^2+x^2)-(x^2-a^2)}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}=\frac{2a^2}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}.$$
Dividing by $a^2+x^2$ gives $\frac{2a^2}{(a^2+x^2)^{3/2}}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{2a^2}{(a^2+x^2)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$**

solutions.title: Check with numbers
solutions.body:
Let $a=x=1$: the numerator is $\sqrt2-0=\sqrt2$ and the fraction is $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$. This rules out (A), (B) and (E), which give $0$, $1$, $1$; (C) and (D) both give $\frac{2}{2^{3/2}}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$. Now try $a=1,x=0$: the fraction is $\frac{1-(-1)}{1}=2$; (D) gives $2$ but (C) gives $0$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{2a^2}{(a^2+x^2)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$**

prompt: The value of $x$ at the intersection of $y=\frac{8}{x^2+4}$ and $x+y=2$ is:

solutions.title: Substitute
solutions.body:
Put $y=2-x$: $(2-x)(x^2+4)=8$, i.e. $2x^2+8-x^3-4x=8$, so $x^3-2x^2+4x=0$, i.e. $x(x^2-2x+4)=0$. The quadratic has discriminant $4-16<0$, so the only real solution is $x=0$ (and then $y=2$, which checks: $8/4=2$).

**Answer: (C) $0$**

prompt: The number of ounces of water needed to reduce $9$ ounces of shaving lotion containing $50\%$ alcohol to a lotion containing $30\%$ alcohol is:

solutions.title: Alcohol stays the same
solutions.body:
The lotion contains $0.5\cdot 9=4.5$ ounces of alcohol. For this to be $30\%$ of the total, the total must be $4.5/0.3=15$ ounces. So add $15-9=6$ ounces of water.

**Answer: (D) $6$**

solutions.title: Equation
solutions.body:
With $w$ ounces of water: $\frac{4.5}{9+w}=0.3\Rightarrow 4.5=2.7+0.3w\Rightarrow w=6.$

**Answer: (D) $6$**

prompt: The number of revolutions of a wheel, with fixed center and with an outside diameter of $6$ feet, required to cause a point on the rim to go one mile is:

solutions.title: Circumference
solutions.body:
One revolution moves a rim point $\pi\cdot 6=6\pi$ feet. One mile is $5280$ feet, so the number of revolutions is $\frac{5280}{6\pi}=\frac{880}{\pi}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{880}{\pi}$**

prompt: A running track is the ring formed by two concentric circles. It is $10$ feet wide. The circumferences of the two circles differ by about:

solutions.title: Difference of circumferences
solutions.body:
If the radii are $R$ and $r=R-10$, the circumferences differ by $2\pi R-2\pi r=2\pi\cdot 10=20\pi\approx 62.8$ feet, about $60$ feet. (It doesn't depend on the size of the track!)

**Answer: (C) 60 feet**

prompt: The diameters of two circles are $8$ inches and $12$ inches respectively. The ratio of the area of the smaller to the area of the larger circle is:

solutions.title: Areas scale as squares
solutions.body:
The ratio of diameters is $\frac{8}{12}=\frac23$, so the ratio of areas is $\left(\frac23\right)^2=\frac49$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{4}{9}$**

prompt: A triangle and a trapezoid are equal in area. They also have the same altitude. If the base of the triangle is $18$ inches, the median of the trapezoid is:

solutions.title: Compare area formulas
solutions.body:
Triangle: area $=\frac12\cdot18\cdot h=9h$. Trapezoid: area $=(\text{median})\cdot h$. Equal areas give median $=9$ inches.

**Answer: (B) 9 inches**

prompt: Given the larger of two circles with center $P$ and radius $p$ and the smaller with center $Q$ and radius $q$. Draw $PQ$. Which of the following statements is false?

solutions.title: Check each position
solutions.body:
- $PQ=p-q$: the circles are internally tangent — possible.
- $PQ=p+q$: externally tangent — possible.
- $PQ>p+q$: the circles are separate — possible.
- $PQ>p-q$: e.g. intersecting or separate circles — possible.

All four statements are true, so none of (A)–(D) is false.

**Answer: (E) none of these**

prompt: A circular piece of metal of maximum size is cut out of a square piece and then a square piece of maximum size is cut out of the circular piece. The total amount of metal wasted is:

choices.text: $\frac{1}{4}$ the area of the original square
$\frac{1}{2}$ the area of the original square
$\frac{1}{2}$ the area of the circular piece
$\frac{1}{4}$ the area of the circular piece

solutions.title: Pick a size
solutions.body:
Let the original square have side $2$ (area $4$). The largest circle has radius $1$. The largest square inside that circle has diagonal $2$, so area $\frac{2^2}{2}=2$.

The final square has area $2$, so the waste is $4-2=2$, which is $\frac12$ of the original square.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{1}{2}$ the area of the original square**

solutions.title: Rotate the inner square
solutions.body:
The inner square's vertices touch the circle, which touches the midpoints of the original square's sides. So the inner square joins the midpoints of the big square's sides; its diagonals cut the big square into 8 congruent triangles, of which the inner square contains 4. It has half the area, so half the metal is wasted.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{1}{2}$ the area of the original square**

prompt: Adams plans a profit of $10\%$ on the selling price of an article and his expenses are $15\%$ of sales. The rate of markup on an article that sells for \$5.00 is:

solutions.title: Find the cost
solutions.body:
On a \$5.00 sale, the profit is \$0.50 and expenses are \$0.75, so the markup is \$1.25 and the cost is $5.00-1.25=\$3.75$.

The markup rate (on cost) is $\frac{1.25}{3.75}=\frac13=33\frac13\%$.

**Answer: (D) $33\frac {1}{3}\%$**

solutions.title: In general
solutions.body:
Profit plus expenses is $25\%$ of the selling price $S$, so the cost is $0.75S$ and the markup $0.25S$ is $\frac{0.25}{0.75}=\frac13$ of the cost, whatever the price.

**Answer: (D) $33\frac {1}{3}\%$**

prompt: A man has part of \$4500 invested at $4\%$ and the rest at $6\%$. If his annual return on each investment is the same, the average rate of interest which he realizes on the \$4500 is:

solutions.title: Set up equations
solutions.body:
Let $x$ be at $4\%$ and $4500-x$ at $6\%$. Equal returns: $0.04x=0.06(4500-x)$, so $0.10x=270$, $x=2700$. Each investment returns $0.04\cdot2700=\$108$, total \$216.

The average rate is $\frac{216}{4500}=0.048=4.8\%$.

**Answer: (B) $4.8\%$**

solutions.title: Harmonic mean
solutions.body:
If each part earns the same return $R$, the amounts are $R/0.04$ and $R/0.06$; the average rate is
$$\frac{2R}{R/0.04+R/0.06}=\frac{2}{25+\frac{50}{3}}=\frac{2}{125/3}=\frac{6}{125}=4.8\%.$$

**Answer: (B) $4.8\%$**

prompt: One of the factors of $x^4+4$ is:

solutions.title: Check by division
solutions.body:
$(x^2-2x+2)(x^2+2x+2)=(x^2+2)^2-(2x)^2=x^4+4x^2+4-4x^2=x^4+4$. ✓ (The others fail: $x=-1$ is not a root since $1+4
e0$; $x^2+2$ would need $x^2=-2$ to give roots, but then $x^4+4=8
e0$; similarly $x^2=4$ gives $20
e0$.)

**Answer: (C) $x^2-2x+2$**

prompt: In the expression $xy^2$, the values of $x$ and $y$ are each decreased $25\%$; the value of the expression is:

solutions.title: Multiply the factors
solutions.body:
The new value is $\frac34x\cdot\left(\frac34y\right)^2=\frac{27}{64}xy^2$. The decrease is $1-\frac{27}{64}=\frac{37}{64}$ of its value.

**Answer: (C) decreased $\frac{37}{64}$ of its value**

prompt: If $y=x+\frac{1}{x}$, then $x^4+x^3-4x^2+x+1=0$ becomes:

solutions.title: Divide by $x^2$
solutions.body:
$x^4+x^3-4x^2+x+1=x^2\left(x^2+\frac1{x^2}+x+\frac1x-4\right)$. Since $y^2=x^2+2+\frac1{x^2}$, we have $x^2+\frac1{x^2}=y^2-2$, so the bracket is $y^2-2+y-4=y^2+y-6$.

**Answer: (D) $x^2(y^2+y-6)=0$**

prompt: If $\log_{10} (x^2-3x+6)=1$, the value of $x$ is:

solutions.title: Remove the log
solutions.body:
$x^2-3x+6=10\Rightarrow x^2-3x-4=0\Rightarrow (x-4)(x+1)=0$, so $x=4$ or $x=-1$. Both make the argument $10>0$, so both are valid.

**Answer: (D) $4$ or $-1$**

prompt: The logarithm of $27\sqrt[4]{9}\sqrt[3]{9}$ to the base $3$ is:
The equation $\sqrt {x + 10} - \frac {6}{\sqrt {x + 10}} = 5$ has:

solutions.title: Substitute $u=\sqrt{x+10}$
solutions.body:
Then $u-\frac6u=5$, i.e. $u^2-5u-6=0$, so $u=6$ or $u=-1$.

- $u=6$: $x=26$, a true root (it is not between $20$ and $25$).
- $u=-1$ is impossible for a square root, but squaring would give $x+10=1$, $x=-9$: an extraneous root between $-10$ and $-6$.

**Answer: (B) an extraneous root between $-10$ and $-6$**

solutions.title: Clear fractions and square
solutions.body:
Multiplying by $\sqrt{x+10}$: $x+10-6=5\sqrt{x+10}$, i.e. $x+4=5\sqrt{x+10}$. Squaring: $x^2+8x+16=25x+250$, $x^2-17x-234=0$, $(x-26)(x+9)=0$. Check: $x=26$ works ($6-1=5$); $x=-9$ gives $1-6=-5\ne5$, so it is extraneous and lies between $-10$ and $-6$.

**Answer: (B) an extraneous root between $-10$ and $-6$**

prompt: If $a,b,c$ are positive integers less than $10$, then $(10a + b)(10a + c) = 100a(a + 1) + bc$ if:

solutions.title: Expand
solutions.body:
$(10a+b)(10a+c)=100a^2+10a(b+c)+bc$, and $100a(a+1)+bc=100a^2+100a+bc$. These are equal exactly when $10a(b+c)=100a$, i.e. $b+c=10$. (This is the trick for $23\cdot27=621$: $2\cdot3=6$, then $3\cdot7=21$.)

**Answer: (A) $b + c = 10$**

prompt: In a geometric progression whose terms are positive, any term is equal to the sum of the next two following terms. Then the common ratio is:

solutions.title: Set up the equation
solutions.body:
With terms $a, ar, ar^2$: $a=ar+ar^2$, so $r^2+r-1=0$ and $r=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt5}{2}$. The terms are positive, so $r>0$: $r=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$**

prompt: The base of a triangle is $15$ inches. Two lines are drawn parallel to the base, terminating in the other two sides, and dividing the triangle into three equal areas. The length of the parallel closer to the base is:

solutions.title: Similar triangles
solutions.body:
The parallel closer to the base cuts off (at the top) a triangle similar to the whole one with $\frac23$ of its area. Lengths scale by the square root of the area ratio, so the parallel has length $15\sqrt{\frac23}=15\cdot\frac{\sqrt6}{3}=5\sqrt6$ inches.

**Answer: (A) $5\sqrt{6}$ inches**

prompt: The radius of the first circle is $1$ inch, that of the second $\frac{1}{2}$ inch, that of the third $\frac{1}{4}$ inch and so on indefinitely. The sum of the areas of the circles is:

solutions.title: Geometric series
solutions.body:
The areas are $\pi,\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{\pi}{16},\dots$, a geometric series with ratio $\frac14$. Its sum is $\frac{\pi}{1-\frac14}=\frac{4\pi}{3}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{4\pi}{3}$**

prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, sides $a,b$ and $c$ are opposite $\angle{A},\angle{B}$ and $\angle{C}$ respectively. $AD$ bisects $\angle{A}$ and meets $BC$ at $D$. Then if $x = \overline{CD}$ and $y = \overline{BD}$ the correct proportion is:

solutions.title: Angle bisector theorem
solutions.body:
The bisector divides $BC$ in the ratio of the adjacent sides: $\frac{x}{y}=\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{b}{c}$ (so (E) is wrong). With $x+y=a$: $y=\frac{ac}{b+c}$, $x=\frac{ab}{b+c}$. Then $\frac{y}{c}=\frac{a}{b+c}$, which is (D).

**Answer: (D) $\frac{y}{c}=\frac{a}{b+c}$**

prompt: The number of significant digits in the measurement of the side of a square whose computed area is $1.1025$ square inches to the nearest ten-thousandth of a square inch is:

solutions.title: Significant digits
solutions.body:
The area $1.1025$ is given to $5$ significant digits. A side computed from it, $\sqrt{1.1025}=1.05$, is treated as having the same precision as the measurement, i.e. $5$ significant digits ($1.0500$ inches).

(This is the answer of the official key: a measured quantity and the area computed from it are taken to have the same number of significant digits.)

**Answer: (D) $5$**

prompt: A house worth \$9000 is sold by Mr. A to Mr. B at a $10\%$ loss. Mr. B sells the house back to Mr. A at a $10\%$ gain. The result of the two transactions is:

solutions.title: Follow the money
solutions.body:
Mr. A sells for $0.9\cdot9000=\$8100$. Mr. B sells back at a $10\%$ gain on his cost: $1.1\cdot8100=\$8910$.

Mr. A ends with the same house, having received \$8100 and paid \$8910: he loses \$810 (and Mr. B gains \$810).

**Answer: (D) Mr. A loses \$810**

prompt: The rails on a railroad are $30$ feet long. As the train passes over the point where the rails are joined, there is an audible click. The speed of the train in miles per hour is approximately the number of clicks heard in:

solutions.title: Convert units
solutions.body:
At $v$ mph the train goes $\frac{5280v}{3600}=\frac{22v}{15}$ feet per second, so it makes $\frac{22v}{15\cdot30}=\frac{22v}{450}$ clicks per second. The number of clicks equals $v$ after $\frac{450}{22}\approx20.5$ seconds, about $20$ seconds.

**Answer: (A) 20 seconds**

solutions.title: Try a speed
solutions.body:
At $30$ mph $=44$ ft/s, there are $\frac{44}{30}\approx1.47$ clicks per second; in $20$ seconds that is about $29$ clicks $\approx30$. ✓

**Answer: (A) 20 seconds**

prompt: Each angle of a rectangle is trisected. The intersections of the pairs of trisectors adjacent to the same side always form:

choices.text: a quadrilateral with no special properties

solutions.title: Symmetry
solutions.body:
The trisectors adjacent to a side make $30^\circ$ angles with that side, at both ends. So over each side they meet at the apex of an isosceles triangle with base angles $30^\circ$, lying on the perpendicular bisector of that side.

For rectangle $ABCD$ centred at $O$, with sides $2w$ (horizontal) and $2h$, the points over the horizontal sides are at distance $h-w\tan30^\circ$ from $O$ vertically, and those over the vertical sides at $w-h\tan30^\circ$ horizontally. Four points on two perpendicular axes, symmetric about $O$, form a quadrilateral whose diagonals are perpendicular and bisect each other: a rhombus. (It is a square only when the rectangle is a square.)

**Answer: (D) a rhombus**

prompt: The perimeter of an isosceles right triangle is $2p$. Its area is:

solutions.title: Find the leg
solutions.body:
With legs $a$, the hypotenuse is $a\sqrt2$, so $a(2+\sqrt2)=2p$ and $a=\frac{2p}{2+\sqrt2}=p(2-\sqrt2)$.

Area $=\frac{a^2}{2}=\frac{p^2(6-4\sqrt2)}{2}=(3-2\sqrt2)p^2$.

**Answer: (C) $(3-2\sqrt{2})p^2$**

solutions.title: Check dimensions and size
solutions.body:
An area must be a multiple of $p^2$, ruling out (A), (B). (D) is negative. (E) $\approx5.8p^2$ is far too big: each leg is less than $p$, so the area is less than $\frac{p^2}{2}$. (C) $\approx0.17p^2$ fits.

**Answer: (C) $(3-2\sqrt{2})p^2$**

prompt: If one side of a triangle is $12$ inches and the opposite angle is $30^{\circ}$, then the diameter of the circumscribed circle is:

solutions.title: Extended law of sines
solutions.body:
$\frac{a}{\sin A}=2R$, so the diameter is $\frac{12}{\sin30^\circ}=24$ inches.

**Answer: (C) 24 inches**

solutions.title: Central angle
solutions.body:
The side of length $12$ subtends an inscribed angle of $30^\circ$, so it subtends a central angle of $60^\circ$. The triangle formed by the centre and that side is equilateral, so the radius is $12$ and the diameter $24$.

**Answer: (C) 24 inches**

prompt: If $f(x)=\frac{x(x-1)}{2}$, then $f(x+2)$ equals:
Determine $m$ so that $4x^2-6x+m$ is divisible by $x-3$. The obtained value, $m$, is an exact divisor of:

solutions.title: Factor theorem
solutions.body:
$x=3$ must be a root: $36-18+m=0$, so $m=-18$. Among the choices, only $36$ is divisible by $18$.

**Answer: (C) $36$**

prompt: The base of an isosceles triangle is $6$ inches and one of the equal sides is $12$ inches. The radius of the circle through the vertices of the triangle is:

solutions.title: $R=\frac{abc}{4K}$
solutions.body:
The altitude to the base is $\sqrt{144-9}=3\sqrt{15}$, so the area is $K=\frac12\cdot6\cdot3\sqrt{15}=9\sqrt{15}$. Then
$$R=\frac{6\cdot12\cdot12}{4\cdot9\sqrt{15}}=\frac{24}{\sqrt{15}}=\frac{8\sqrt{15}}{5}\approx6.20,$$
which is none of the listed values.

**Answer: (E) none of these**

solutions.title: Centre on the altitude
solutions.body:
Put the base from $(-3,0)$ to $(3,0)$ and apex at $(0,3\sqrt{15})$. The centre $(0,k)$ satisfies $9+k^2=(3\sqrt{15}-k)^2=135-6\sqrt{15}k+k^2$, so $k=\frac{126}{6\sqrt{15}}=\frac{21}{\sqrt{15}}$ and $R=3\sqrt{15}-k=\frac{45-21}{\sqrt{15}}=\frac{24}{\sqrt{15}}$. Not among (A)–(D).

**Answer: (E) none of these**

prompt: If $f(a)=a-2$ and $F(a,b)=b^2+a$, then $F(3,f(4))$ is:
The product $\log_a b \cdot \log_b a$ is equal to:

solutions.title: Change of base
solutions.body:
$\log_ab\cdot\log_ba=\frac{\log b}{\log a}\cdot\frac{\log a}{\log b}=1.$

**Answer: (A) $1$**

prompt: The negation of the statement “all men are honest” is:

solutions.title: Negating “all”
solutions.body:
“All men are honest” is false exactly when at least one man is not honest. So the negation is “some men are dishonest”. (“No men are honest” is too strong — it is not the negation.)

**Answer: (C) some men are dishonest**

prompt: A girls' camp is located $300$ rods from a straight road. On this road, a boys' camp is located $500$ rods from the girls' camp. It is desired to build a canteen on the road which shall be exactly the same distance from each camp. The distance of the canteen from each of the camps is:

solutions.title: Coordinates
solutions.body:
Let the road be the $x$-axis, the girls' camp $G=(0,300)$. The boys' camp is on the road at distance $500$: $B=(400,0)$ (a 3-4-5 triangle). The canteen $C=(x,0)$ satisfies $x^2+300^2=(400-x)^2$, so $90000=160000-800x$ and $x=87.5$.

The distance is $400-87.5=312.5$ rods — not in the list.

**Answer: (E) none of these**

solutions.title: Similar triangles
solutions.body:
The canteen lies on the perpendicular bisector of $GB$. Let $F=(0,0)$ be the foot from $G$ and $M$ the midpoint of $GB$, $GM=250$. Triangles $BMC$ and $BFG$ are similar (right angles at $M$, $F$, common angle $B$), so $\frac{BC}{BG}=\frac{BM}{BF}$: $BC=\frac{500\cdot250}{400}=312.5$ rods.

**Answer: (E) none of these**

prompt: The centers of two circles are $41$ inches apart. The smaller circle has a radius of $4$ inches and the larger one has a radius of $5$ inches. The length of the common internal tangent is:

solutions.title: Shift the tangent
solutions.body:
For an internal tangent, slide it parallel to itself until it passes through the smaller circle's centre. It forms a right triangle with hypotenuse $41$ (the distance between centres) and one leg $4+5=9$. The tangent length is $\sqrt{41^2-9^2}=\sqrt{1600}=40$ inches.

**Answer: (E) 40 inches**

prompt: If the price of an article is increased by percent $p$, then the decrease in percent of sales must not exceed $d$ in order to yield the same income. The value of $d$ is:

solutions.title: Income equation
solutions.body:
Treat $p$ and $d$ as fractions. Income is price $\times$ sales: $(1+p)(1-d)=1$, so $1-d=\frac{1}{1+p}$ and $d=\frac{p}{1+p}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{p}{1+p}$**

solutions.title: Example
solutions.body:
If the price rises $25\%$ ($p=\frac14$), sales may fall to $\frac{1}{1.25}=0.8$, i.e. by $20\%=\frac{1/4}{5/4}$. ✓

**Answer: (C) $\frac{p}{1+p}$**

prompt: In solving a problem that reduces to a quadratic equation one student makes a mistake only in the constant term of the equation and obtains $8$ and $2$ for the roots. Another student makes a mistake only in the coefficient of the first degree term and finds $-9$ and $-1$ for the roots. The correct equation was:

solutions.title: Vieta's formulas
solutions.body:
For $x^2+bx+c=0$, the sum of roots is $-b$ and the product is $c$. The first student has the correct $b$: sum $8+2=10$, so $b=-10$. The second has the correct $c$: product $(-9)(-1)=9$. The equation is $x^2-10x+9=0$.

**Answer: (A) $x^2-10x+9=0$**

prompt: The lengths of two line segments are $a$ units and $b$ units respectively. Then the correct relation between them is:

solutions.title: AM–GM
solutions.body:
Since $a,b>0$: $\frac{a+b}{2}-\sqrt{ab}=\frac{(\sqrt a-\sqrt b)^2}{2}\ge0$, with equality when $a=b$. So $\frac{a+b}2\ge\sqrt{ab}$ always; (A) fails when $a=b$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{a+b}{2}\geq\sqrt{ab}$**

prompt: Instead of walking along two adjacent sides of a rectangular field, a boy took a shortcut along the diagonal of the field and saved a distance equal to $\frac{1}{2}$ the longer side. The ratio of the shorter side of the rectangle to the longer side was:

solutions.title: Set up the equation
solutions.body:
Shorter side $a$, longer $b$: $a+b-\sqrt{a^2+b^2}=\frac b2$, so $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}=a+\frac b2$. Squaring: $a^2+b^2=a^2+ab+\frac{b^2}4$, so $\frac34b^2=ab$ and $\frac ab=\frac34$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{3}{4}$**

solutions.title: 3-4-5 check
solutions.body:
With sides $3$ and $4$ the diagonal is $5$: walking the sides is $7$, the diagonal saves $2=\frac12\cdot4$. ✓

**Answer: (D) $\frac{3}{4}$**

prompt: If $x>0$, then the correct relationship is:

solutions.title: Compare growth
solutions.body:
Let $g(x)=x-\ln(1+x)$. Then $g(0)=0$ and $g'(x)=1-\frac1{1+x}=\frac{x}{1+x}>0$ for $x>0$, so $g(x)>0$: $\ln(1+x)<x$. (For common logarithms, $\log(1+x)<\ln(1+x)<x$ as well.)

Also $\ln(1+x)>\frac{x}{1+x}$ for $x>0$ (same method), so (A), (B) fail and (C) fails too.

**Answer: (D) $\log (1+x) < x$**

solutions.title: Exponential view
solutions.body:
$e^x>1+x$ for $x\neq0$ (the tangent line at $0$ lies below the convex curve $e^x$). Taking logarithms, $x>\ln(1+x)$.

**Answer: (D) $\log (1+x) < x$**

prompt: If the larger base of an isosceles trapezoid equals a diagonal and the smaller base equals the altitude, then the ratio of the smaller base to the larger base is:

solutions.title: Right triangle from a diagonal
solutions.body:
Let the larger base be $B$, the smaller base $b$ (also the altitude). Drop a perpendicular from an upper vertex: a diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $b$ (height) and $\frac{B+b}{2}$ (horizontal run). So
$$B^2=\left(\frac{B+b}{2}\right)^2+b^2.$$
With $r=\frac bB$: $4=(1+r)^2+4r^2$, i.e. $5r^2+2r-3=0=(5r-3)(r+1)$, so $r=\frac35$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{3}{5}$**

solutions.title: Check
solutions.body:
Take $B=5$, $b=3$: the run is $4$, height $3$, diagonal $\sqrt{16+9}=5=B$. ✓

**Answer: (D) $\frac{3}{5}$**

prompt: The coordinates of $A,B$ and $C$ are $(5,5),(2,1)$ and $(0,k)$ respectively. The value of $k$ that makes $\overline{AC}+\overline{BC}$ as small as possible is:

solutions.title: Reflect across the $y$-axis
solutions.body:
Reflect $A$ to $A'=(-5,5)$; then $AC=A'C$, and $A'C+CB$ is smallest when $C$ lies on segment $A'B$. The line through $(-5,5)$ and $(2,1)$ has slope $-\frac47$; at $x=0$: $y=5-\frac47\cdot5=\frac{15}7=2\frac17$.

**Answer: (E) $2\frac{1}{7}$**

prompt: One of the sides of a triangle is divided into segments of $6$ and $8$ units by the point of tangency of the inscribed circle. If the radius of the circle is $4$, then the length of the shortest side of the triangle is:

solutions.title: Heron's formula
solutions.body:
Tangent lengths from the vertices are $6$, $8$, and some $z$. The sides are $14$, $6+z$, $8+z$, and $s=14+z$. Area $=rs=4(14+z)$, and by Heron, area $=\sqrt{s\cdot z\cdot 6\cdot 8}$. So $16(14+z)^2=48z(14+z)$, giving $14+z=3z$, $z=7$.

The sides are $14,13,15$; the shortest is $13$.

**Answer: (B) 13 units**

solutions.title: Half-angle tangents
solutions.body:
At the vertices with tangent lengths $6$ and $8$, $\tan\frac{\alpha}2=\frac46$ and $\tan\frac\beta2=\frac48$. The third half-angle is $90^\circ-\frac\alpha2-\frac\beta2$, so $\tan\frac\gamma2=\cot\left(\frac\alpha2+\frac\beta2\right)=\frac{1-\frac23\cdot\frac12}{\frac23+\frac12}=\frac{2/3}{7/6}=\frac47$, giving tangent length $z=\frac{4}{4/7}=7$. Sides $13,14,15$.

**Answer: (B) 13 units**

prompt: The square of $5-\sqrt{y^2-25}$ is:

The equation $\frac{2x^2}{x-1}-\frac{2x+7}{3}+\frac{4-6x}{x-1}+1=0$ can be transformed by eliminating fractions to the equation $x^2-5x+4=0$. The roots of the latter equation are $4$ and $1$. Then the roots of the first equation are:

solutions.title: Check for division by zero
solutions.body:
The original equation has $x-1$ in denominators, so $x=1$ is not allowed: it is an extraneous root introduced by multiplying by $x-1$. The value $x=4$ makes no denominator zero, so it is a genuine root, and since the cleared equation has only roots $4$ and $1$, the only root is $4$.

(Check: $\frac{32}{3}-5+\frac{-20}{3}+1=4-4=0$. ✓)

**Answer: (C) only $4$**

prompt: If $x$ varies as the cube of $y$, and $y$ varies as the fifth root of $z$, then $x$ varies as the $n$th power of $z$, where $n$ is:

solutions.title: Substitute
solutions.body:
$x=ky^3$ and $y=mz^{1/5}$, so $x=km^3z^{3/5}$. Hence $n=\frac35$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{3}{5}$**

prompt: If the Highest Common Divisor of $6432$ and $132$ is diminished by $8$, it will equal:

solutions.title: Prime factors
solutions.body:
$132=2^2\cdot3\cdot11$ and $6432=2^5\cdot3\cdot67$. The common part is $2^2\cdot3=12$; $12-8=4$.

**Answer: (E) $4$**

prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius $10$ inches. Its area is:

solutions.title: Six equilateral triangles
solutions.body:
The hexagon splits into $6$ equilateral triangles of side $10$ (the radius). Each has area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot100=25\sqrt3$, so the hexagon has area $150\sqrt3$ sq. in.

**Answer: (A) $150\sqrt{3}$ sq. in.**

prompt: The value of $\frac{1}{16}a^0+\left (\frac{1}{16a} \right )^0- \left (64^{-\frac{1}{2}} \right )- (-32)^{-\frac{4}{5}}$ is:
A housewife saved \$2.50 in buying a dress on sale. If she spent \$25 for the dress, she saved about:

solutions.title: Percent of the original price
solutions.body:
The original price was $25+2.50=\$27.50$. She saved $\frac{2.50}{27.50}=\frac1{11}\approx9.1\%$, about $9\%$.

**Answer: (B) $9\%$**

prompt: The base of a triangle is twice as long as a side of a square and their areas are the same. Then the ratio of the altitude of the triangle to the side of the square is:

solutions.title: Compare areas
solutions.body:
With square side $s$, the triangle has base $2s$ and altitude $h$: $\frac12\cdot2s\cdot h=s^2$, so $h=s$ and the ratio is $1$.

**Answer: (C) $1$**

prompt: A point $P$ is outside a circle and is $13$ inches from the center. A secant from $P$ cuts the circle at $Q$ and $R$ so that the external segment of the secant $PQ$ is $9$ inches and $QR$ is $7$ inches. The radius of the circle is:

solutions.title: Power of a point
solutions.body:
$PQ\cdot PR=9\cdot16=144$. Also, along the line through the centre, the power of $P$ is $(13-r)(13+r)=169-r^2$. So $169-r^2=144$ and $r=5$ inches.

**Answer: (C) 5 in.**

solutions.title: Coordinates of the chord
solutions.body:
The midpoint $M$ of chord $QR$ is $9+3.5=12.5$ from $P$, and $OM\perp QR$. In right triangle $OMP$: $OM^2=13^2-12.5^2=12.75$. In right triangle $OMQ$: $r^2=OM^2+3.5^2=12.75+12.25=25$, so $r=5$.

**Answer: (C) 5 in.**

prompt: The sum of the numerical coefficients in the expansion of the binomial $(a+b)^6$ is:

solutions.title: Set $a=b=1$
solutions.body:
The sum of the coefficients is the value at $a=b=1$: $(1+1)^6=64$.

**Answer: (C) $64$**

solutions.title: Pascal's row
solutions.body:
The coefficients are $1,6,15,20,15,6,1$, which add up to $64$.

**Answer: (C) $64$**

prompt: A merchant placed on display some dresses, each with a marked price. He then posted a sign “$\frac{1}{3}$ off on these dresses.” The cost of the dresses was $\frac{3}{4}$ of the price at which he actually sold them. Then the ratio of the cost to the marked price was:

solutions.title: Chain the fractions
solutions.body:
The selling price is $\frac23$ of the marked price, and the cost is $\frac34$ of that: $\frac34\cdot\frac23=\frac12$ of the marked price.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{1}{2}$**

solutions.title: Use a number
solutions.body:
Marked price \$12: sold for \$8; cost $\frac34\cdot8=\$6$; ratio $\frac6{12}=\frac12$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{1}{2}$**

prompt: The solution of the equations $$\begin{aligned}2x-3y &=7 \\ 4x-6y &=20\end{aligned}$$ is:

choices.text: There are an unlimited number of solutions

solutions.title: Compare the equations
solutions.body:
Doubling the first equation gives $4x-6y=14$, but the second says $4x-6y=20$. Both can't hold, so there is no solution (the lines are parallel).

**Answer: (C) There is no solution**

prompt: A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. If angles are inscribed in the four arcs cut off by the sides of the quadrilateral, their sum will be:

solutions.title: Inscribed angle theorem
solutions.body:
Let the four arcs be $a,b,c,d$ with $a+b+c+d=360^\circ$. An angle inscribed in arc $a$ (vertex on that arc) intercepts the rest of the circle, so it measures $\frac{360^\circ-a}{2}$. The sum is
$$\frac{4\cdot360^\circ-(a+b+c+d)}{2}=\frac{1440^\circ-360^\circ}{2}=540^\circ.$$

**Answer: (B) $540^\circ$**

solutions.title: Special case
solutions.body:
Take a square: each arc is $90^\circ$, and an angle inscribed in it intercepts $270^\circ$, so measures $135^\circ$. Four of them: $540^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $540^\circ$**

prompt: When simplified $\sqrt{1+ \left (\frac{x^4-1}{2x^2} \right )^2}$ equals:

solutions.title: Test $x=1$
solutions.body:
The expression is $\sqrt{1+0}=1$. (A) gives $1$, (B) $0$, (C) $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$, (D) $\frac1{\sqrt2}$, (E) $1$. Try $x^2=2$: expression $\sqrt{1+(3/4)^2}=\frac54$; (A) gives $\frac{7}{4}$, (E) gives $1+\frac14=\frac54$. ✓

**Answer: (E) $\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{1}{2x^2}$**

prompt: $\log 125$ equals:

solutions.title: Use $5=10/2$
solutions.body:
$\log125=3\log5=3\log\frac{10}{2}=3(1-\log2)=3-3\log2$ (common logarithms).

**Answer: (D) $3 - 3\log 2$**

prompt: If $f(x) = 5x^2 - 2x - 1$, then $f(x + h) - f(x)$ equals:

solutions.title: Check $h=0$
solutions.body:
The difference must be $0$ when $h=0$; that rules out (B) and (C). With $x=0,h=1$: $f(1)-f(0)=2-(-1)=3$; (A) gives $3$, (D) gives $3$, (E) gives $3$. With $x=1,h=1$: $f(2)-f(1)=15-2=13$; only (D) gives $10+5-2=13$.

**Answer: (D) $h(10x+5h-2)$**

prompt: The graph of the function $f(x) = 2x^3 - 7$ goes:

choices.text: up to the right and down to the left
down to the right and up to the left
up to the right and up to the left
down to the right and down to the left

solutions.title: End behaviour
solutions.body:
For large positive $x$, $2x^3$ is huge and positive, so the graph rises to the right; for large negative $x$, $2x^3$ is hugely negative, so it falls to the left. (In fact $f$ is increasing everywhere.)

**Answer: (A) up to the right and down to the left**

prompt: Of the following sets, the one that includes all values of $x$ which will satisfy $2x - 3 > 7 - x$ is:

solutions.title: Solve
solutions.body:
$2x-3>7-x\iff 3x>10\iff x>\frac{10}3$. (The set $x>4$ misses solutions such as $x=3.5$.)

**Answer: (D) $x >\frac{10}{3}$**

prompt: If the three points of contact of a circle inscribed in a triangle are joined, the angles of the resulting triangle:

choices.text: are always one obtuse angle and two unequal acute angles
are always one obtuse angle and two equal acute angles
are always unequal to each other

solutions.title: Tangent–chord angles
solutions.body:
Let the incircle touch $BC,CA,AB$ at $D,E,F$. Since $AE=AF$, triangle $AEF$ is isosceles with apex angle $A$, so $\angle AFE=90^\circ-\frac A2$; similarly $\angle BFD=90^\circ-\frac B2$. Then
$$\angle DFE=180^\circ-\left(90^\circ-\tfrac A2\right)-\left(90^\circ-\tfrac B2\right)=\frac{A+B}{2}=90^\circ-\frac C2<90^\circ.$$
Likewise the other two angles are $90^\circ-\frac A2$ and $90^\circ-\frac B2$, all acute. (They are equal to $60^\circ$ only for an equilateral triangle, so (A) and (E) are not always true.)

**Answer: (D) are always acute angles**

prompt: The equation $x^3+6x^2+11x+6=0$ has:

solutions.title: Factor
solutions.body:
$x=-1$ is a root ($-1+6-11+6=0$), and $x^3+6x^2+11x+6=(x+1)(x+2)(x+3)$. The roots are $-1,-2,-3$: no positive real roots.

**Answer: (B) no positive real roots**

solutions.title: Signs
solutions.body:
All coefficients are positive, so for $x>0$ the left side is positive and cannot be $0$. Hence there are no positive roots (and since a cubic has a real root, (C) is false).

**Answer: (B) no positive real roots**

prompt: The roots of the equation $2\sqrt {x} + 2x^{ - \frac {1}{2}} = 5$ can be found by solving:

solutions.title: Multiply by $\sqrt x$
solutions.body:
$2x+2=5\sqrt x$. Squaring: $4x^2+8x+4=25x$, i.e. $4x^2-17x+4=0$. (Its roots $4$ and $\frac14$ both check: $4+1=5$ and $1+4=5$.)

**Answer: (C) $4x^2-17x+4 = 0$**

solutions.title: Substitute $u=\sqrt x$
solutions.body:
$2u+\frac2u=5\Rightarrow 2u^2-5u+2=0\Rightarrow u=2$ or $\frac12$, so $x=4$ or $\frac14$. The quadratic with these roots is $x^2-\frac{17}{4}x+1=0$, i.e. $4x^2-17x+4=0$.

**Answer: (C) $4x^2-17x+4 = 0$**

prompt: The expression $\frac{2x^2-x}{(x+1)(x-2)}-\frac{4+x}{(x+1)(x-2)}$ cannot be evaluated for $x=-1$ or $x=2$, since division by zero is not allowed. For other values of $x$:

choices.text: The expression takes on many different values.
The expression has only the value 2.
The expression has only the value 1.
The expression always has a value between $-1$ and $+2$.
The expression has a value greater than 2 or less than $-1$.

solutions.title: Combine and factor
solutions.body:
$$\frac{2x^2-x-4-x}{(x+1)(x-2)}=\frac{2x^2-2x-4}{(x+1)(x-2)}=\frac{2(x^2-x-2)}{(x+1)(x-2)}=\frac{2(x+1)(x-2)}{(x+1)(x-2)}=2.$$

**Answer: (B) The expression has only the value 2.**

solutions.title: Try $x=0$
solutions.body:
$\frac{0}{-2}-\frac{4}{-2}=2$. And $x=1$: $\frac{1}{-2}-\frac{5}{-2}=2$. It is always $2$.

**Answer: (B) The expression has only the value 2.**

prompt: If the margin made on an article costing $C$ dollars and selling for $S$ dollars is $M=\frac{1}{n}C$, then the margin is given by:

solutions.title: Eliminate $C$
solutions.body:
$S=C+M=nM+M=(n+1)M$, so $M=\frac{S}{n+1}$.

**Answer: (D) $M=\frac{1}{n+1}S$**

prompt: The values of $k$ for which the equation $2x^2-kx+x+8=0$ will have real and equal roots are:

solutions.title: Discriminant zero
solutions.body:
The equation is $2x^2+(1-k)x+8=0$. Equal roots need $(1-k)^2-64=0$, so $1-k=\pm8$: $k=-7$ or $k=9$.

**Answer: (A) $9$ and $-7$**
